as_told.title: Puharich case of metal in teeth picking up signals

plain: In the 1950s or 60s a man who worked with metal is said to have heard voices that turned out to be a radio station, picked up through metal dust lodged in his teeth. The story comes from the work of Andrija Puharich, a scientist who studied the mind and later psychic claims. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells it from the writer Annie Jacobsen's account, calling it Puharich's first "aha moment": a mental patient who said he heard voices was in fact receiving New York's WOR radio station. Jesse Michels tells it several times, crediting Puharich and once a documentary about him. In his versions the man worked in a metal mill or sawmill and fine metal got into his teeth, and Michels does not name the station. Once he links it to the idea that thoughts might be sent by very low frequency radio waves. The tellers raise it because it suggests the body could receive signals directly, which Puharich took as a clue to telepathy.
